meta.topic_profile_source: detective.json topic_profile (is_computational=true AND is_visual=true) — fanned out WIDELY per the computational gate; editor.md/editor.json did not exist yet, so the lead candidate is marked here by the Imagineer.
meta.node_checked: code/client_model.js node-run: reweightRankings + RANK_LOOKUP both return the expected shapes and reproduce analyst.json exactly (balanced #1 Oxford 87.02, qs_like #1 MIT 96.25, output_only #1 Michigan 100; RANK_LOOKUP n=218, Peking 48/101/56/12 works17 cites35 spread89).
meta._doc: Candidate interactive-concept pool for the Editor to curate a hero + supporting set from. img_xx are INTERNAL planning ids — never reach the HTML, tagged on no element, in no provenance tuple. Deliberate over-generation (14 concepts, one per producible finding). Only what the Editor keeps is ever built.

img_01.label: Re-weight the world rankings and watch #1 flip
img_01.reader_produces: drags the five pillar weights (rep/cite/teach/intl/vol) and re-ranks all 218 universities live — manufactures Oxford, MIT, or Michigan as world #1 from the SAME data, discovering 'best university' is a slider position
img_01.sketch: 5 sliders(rep,cite,teach,intl,vol)+preset chips(balanced/qs_like/the_like/arwu_like/output_only) -> animated ranked bars + #1 badge; bare readout = the live #1's blended score

img_02.label: Look up your university's five verdicts
img_02.reader_produces: types a university and pulls its four commercial ranks (THE/ARWU/CWUR/QS) + OpenAlex works & cites ranks + its cross-system spread — 'your uni swings N places between the tables'
img_02.sketch: search <input>/<datalist>(218 names) -> dumbbell/slope of its 4 commercial + 2 OpenAlex ranks; bare readout = the spread number

img_03.label: Guess a famous school's rank spread before the reveal
img_03.reader_produces: commits a guess for where Peking (or Tsinghua/Berkeley) sits in each of the four tables, then feels the real 89-place QS-vs-ARWU gap land data-bound
img_03.sketch: pick a named swinger + guess slider(its QS rank) -> reveal real per-system ranks as data-bound bars (Peking QS12 vs ARWU101); verdict on the spread

img_04.label: Guess each table's #1 - then meet four different champions
img_04.reader_produces: picks who they think tops THE, ARWU, CWUR, QS and OpenAlex, then discovers Caltech / Harvard / MIT / Michigan are four (five) different winners — nobody is #1 everywhere
img_04.sketch: 5 choice rows (candidate tiles: Caltech/Harvard/MIT/Michigan/...) -> score vs the real #1 of each table; reveal the side-by-side top-10 grid

img_05.label: Guess Michigan's impact rank, then watch volume flip to per-paper
img_05.reader_produces: guesses where the raw-output #1 (Michigan) lands once you divide citations by papers, then sees the +331-place plunge from works #1 to per-paper impact #332
img_05.sketch: guess slider(Michigan's per-paper impact rank) -> reveal works#1 vs impact#332 data-bound bars; verdict; bare readout = 332

img_06.label: Pick two systems and see how little they agree
img_06.reader_produces: chooses any two ranking systems and re-derives their agreement — a scatter of all 218 universities' rank-in-A vs rank-in-B plus the Spearman number (0.60 for QS-vs-CWUR, the systematic outlier)
img_06.sketch: two system dropdowns -> scatter of 218 rank-pairs built from RANK_LOOKUP + Spearman r from ana_04 table; bare readout = the selected pair's r (refilter/selector, no live regression needed)

img_07.label: Toggle the referee's lens - the neutral yardstick has three #1s too
img_07.reader_produces: switches OpenAlex between raw volume / total citations / h-index and watches the neutral top-10 crown a different school each time (Michigan -> Harvard -> Washington) — the referee opens a new argument instead of settling it
img_07.sketch: 3 toggle chips(works/cited_by/h_index) -> reordered top-10 list with animated rows; caption = which #1 this lens crowns

img_08.label: Inside QS: the reputation survey and the citation metric disagree
img_08.reader_produces: picks a school and reads its QS Academic-Reputation survey score against its Citations-per-Faculty score, seeing the survey lift reputation-rich names (Peking, HKU) and sink research-dense ones (Vanderbilt, UCSB)
img_08.sketch: school picker (reputation-lifted vs research-lifted lists) -> AR bar vs CPF bar + QS-minus-ARWU gap, on a scatter of AR vs CPF. HIGH on the 20 curated rows in ana_09; a full 218-wide AR-vs-CPF version would need the Analyst to emit per-university QS CPF (reweight model has QS-AR as 'rep' but not QS-CPF) -> that variant is medium

img_09.label: Which table tracks the neutral referee?
img_09.reader_produces: picks a commercial system and an OpenAlex lens and produces how tightly that table tracks measured output — discovering ARWU tracks research most (0.88 vs h-index) and QS tracks impact least (0.64)
img_09.sketch: system chips(THE/ARWU/CWUR/QS) x lens chips(works/cited_by/h_index) -> Spearman value + bar; bare readout = the selected r

img_10.label: Guess how far apart the four tables put a typical school
img_10.reader_produces: commits a guess for the median best-to-worst rank gap across the four systems, then sees it is 122 places — and where their guess sits in the spread distribution
img_10.sketch: numeric guess slider(0-300) -> reveal median 122 + the spread-distribution band (q25 64 / median 122 / q75 210) from ana_05 quantiles; verdict; bare readout = 122

img_11.label: Guess how much of each ranking is just reputation survey
img_11.reader_produces: guesses the reputation-survey share of QS (and the others), then sees QS is 50% surveyed opinion while ARWU and CWUR are 0% — the mechanical reason the tables disagree
img_11.sketch: guess slider(% of QS score that is opinion) -> reveal the stacked weighting bar (reputation vs citations vs output) for all five systems; verdict; bare readout = 50

img_12.label: Flip the whole core between volume and per-paper impact
img_12.reader_produces: slides one assumption from raw-volume weighting to per-paper impact and watches the entire OpenAlex leaderboard invert - sprawling giants (Michigan, Toronto) sink, small dense schools (Caltech, Princeton) rise

needs.client_model: code/client_model.js:reweightRankings (partial: exposes a 'vol' output pillar but NO per-paper-impact field; a full 218-row volume<->per-paper flip needs a cites/work-normalised array the Analyst has not emitted - only ana_10's 11 named rows exist today)

img_12.sketch: single slider(volume <-> per-paper) -> re-ranked full leaderboard; Analyst should emit a per-paper-impact (cites/work) pillar or a normImpact model to make the 218-wide version high (the 11-school named version is high today)

img_13.label: Spin the weights - how many schools can be world #1?
img_13.reader_produces: hits 'spin' to randomise the pillar weights over and over and tallies how many DIFFERENT universities become world #1, feeling that 'best' is a dice roll of what you choose to weight
img_13.sketch: 'spin' button -> random weights -> reweightRankings -> new #1 flashes onto the podium; running tally of DISTINCT #1s as the bare readout (an alternative framing of ana_12 - the Editor will not build this AND the img_01 hero)

img_14.label: Does the disagreement vanish if you compare the same year?
img_14.reader_produces: guesses whether forcing all three tables to 2015 makes them agree, then sees they still correlate only 0.78 - proving the gap is methodology, not the dataset's era-mismatch
img_14.sketch: toggle(mixed-era vs 2015-only trio) + guess slider -> reveal same-year mean Spearman 0.782 vs the reader's ~1.0 prior; bare readout = 0.782
